pairs.why: The two are almost the same; A's lenses are a slightly deeper, calmer blue and it has a bit less polish, which is a little nearer the real viewer.
A adds a glossy, saturated toy base, mirror-like lenses and extra props, while B keeps the calmer, softer finish and simple framing of the real card.
A's rounded blue housing with silver trim matches the real card's colour masses better than B's mostly grey faceplate, and its finish is not much glossier.
A is a chunky, saturated, plastic-looking toy, while B has the calmer yellow and orange wood and the plank build of the real feeder.
A's simpler open box and flat colour read closer to the real feeder than B's arched walls and metal rings, though the two are close.
B adds a hard bracket hanger and bolted, crisper construction, while A's softer rope-hung plank feeder is closer to the real card's look.
A keeps the real calculator's main colours, dark blue keys with a cyan operator column, while B's cream keys change the overall colour, which matters more than A's missing key labels.
As in p185, A's dark blue body with blue keys and cyan operator keys matches the real card's colour masses, while B's white keys read as a different object.
